Subject: POC Trial - Model selection and evaluation plan

Hi Sofia / Diego —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps for the POC so we have alignment before we start: 

High-level objective:
- Validate that Redwood can deliver sub-300ms token latency for live triage flows and hit >= 92% intent classification accuracy on your triage prompts, while supporting Spanish and Portuguese traffic.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: median request-to-first-token < 300ms under target concurrency (10 rps)
2) Quality: intent classification / routing accuracy >= 92% on an agreed holdout prompt set
3) Robustness: graceful fallback to a cheaper model under load with <1% user-visible degradation
4) Security: PII-handling and audit logs enabled; no customer data stored outside your VPC for Private runs (if we go Private)

Evaluation plan / deliverables:
- Redwood provides a POC environment (hosted dedicated pool) with two model variants: primary and fallback.
- We’ll run a 2-week trial with: week 1 integration + smoke tests; week 2 load/quality run and eval.
- Customer provides ~1k representative prompts (anonymized) + sample traffic profile by EOD Jul 8.
- Redwood returns a results report with throughput/latency, per-intent accuracy, token cost estimates, and recommended quantization profile.

Timeline (proposed):
- Jul 8: Customer sample data + confirm NDA status
- Jul 9–11: Redwood prepares trial infra + model configs
- Jul 12: Kickoff + integration window starts
- Jul 19: End of trial + delivery of results and recommendations

Ownership:
- Customer PM: Sofia Ramos (Acme Health) — data & acceptance
- Customer data owner: Diego Alvarez — sample data, schema
- Redwood PM: Marissa Cole — project management, reporting
- Redwood SE: Aditya Rao — technical lead, model selection, tuning

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Confirm multilingual coverage beyond Spanish/Portuguese (any other locales?).
- Any PII redaction requirements or data retention constraints we should know about?
- Are you ok with an initial open-model selection (we assume Llama-2-13b-chat family or Mistral variants) or do you need us to avoid certain vendor-licensed models?

I attached a short POC template (redwood-poc-template.xlsx) that outlines the data contract and test cases. Please confirm the success criteria and share the sample prompts by Jul 8 so we can lock the schedule.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is very clear and captures the call well. A few confirmations from our side: 

- Success criteria: we agree on the latency and accuracy targets. The 92% accuracy is on the intent routing task specifically (not on downstream classification).
- Languages: primary traffic will be English (~60%), Spanish (~30%), Portuguese (~10%). We don’t have other locales for the initial POC.
- Data: I’ll share an anonymized sample set (1k prompts) and a simple schema dump by Jul 8. Diego will send the CSV.
- Compliance: we have a standing DPA; we’ll surface any retention limits but initial POC data should be fine to process.

Model constraints: we prefer open-source models or permissive licenses for the POC. Avoid commercial-only LLMs that require enterprise licenses if possible. If you recommend a commercial variant, please call it out as an optional high-performance fallback.

I attached a short scope doc for internal review (Acme_POCT_scope.pdf).

Hi all — quick note on model selection and a suggested config for the trial based on the multilingual requirement and cost/latency tradeoffs: 

Primary recommendation (open model):
- Llama-2-13b-chat (quantized q4_0 or q4_k_m) — good tradeoff for instruction-following and decent Spanish/Portuguese handling. Works well with k/v cache optimizations in our runtime for low-latency chat-style prompts.

Fallback (cheaper, faster):
- Mistral-7b-instruct (int8) — lower cost per token and faster in many cases; good for fallback routing where extreme fidelity is not required.

Optional high-performance (call out as commercial):
- Falcon-40B-instruct or Llama-3 variants — higher quality on multilingual benchmarks but may have licensing constraints. We can surface those as a premium option.

Notes and eval plan specifics:
- Tokenization: we'll run a tokenization pass on your sample prompts and report per-language token counts — this will inform cost estimates.
- Prompting: we'll standardize a small prompt template for intent routing and generate an evaluation harness of ~200 holdout prompts across intents and languages.
- Metrics: top-1 intent accuracy, confusion matrix by intent, median latency (p50/p95), and cost per 1k requests.
- Quantization profile: we'll test q4_0 and q4_k_m for Llama-2-13b-chat and compare quality delta (<2% accuracy degradation target).

Operational notes:
- We'll enable prefix KV caching for repeated session flows to reduce end-to-end latency.
- For the fallback policy, we recommend a latency-headroom rule: if p95 latency > 400ms on the primary under load, route new requests to Mistral-7b until recovery.

Happy to sync on a quick 30-min technical kickoff when you share the sample data.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
